transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-07
Start time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Nina Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Ravi Menon (Helios CTO), Elena Castillo (Helios Cloud Architect), Tom Brewer (Helios Marketplace PM), Sofia Alvarez (Helios Security)

Summary: quick technical sync to align on deployment patterns for the joint solution, checklist items for listing readiness, packaging formats (AMI vs container), and pilot scope. Action items and follow-ups captured at end.

Topics: deployment topology options, packaging artifacts, marketplace listing requirements, billing and metering questions, security and certs, pilot test plan

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Nina Patel: Okay everyone, thanks for joining. I think we've got about 50 minutes, so let's run through the agenda. Marcus and I will cover the Redwood packaging and listing constraints, then we want to walk through Helios's preferred deployment topology and the pilot plan.
[00:18] Ravi Menon: Sounds good. Sorry, had to pull in Sofia last minute for security questions, and Tom for the marketplace pieces.
[00:25] Marcus Li: Hey all. Quick note, apologies in advance for the background noise at my side.
[00:30] Elena Castillo: No worries. We may go into networking details so heads up.
[00:36] Nina Patel: Great. Marcus, can you start with the packaging options and what Redwood expects for a marketplace listing?
[00:42] Marcus Li: Sure. So for listings we typically accept two packaging patterns: an AMI-based image for private on-cloud deployment or a container image with a deployment bundle. The AMI route is common in cloud marketplaces for dedicated instances, whereas container bundles are used for marketplace listings that deploy into customer clusters via provided Helm charts or Terraform. We have a checklist, it's a PDF I'll share - listing-checklist.pdf.
[01:06] Tom Brewer: Quick question, is AMI required for the public cloud listing? Our product team prefers container-first.
[01:12] Nina Patel: It's not strictly required. Depends on the marketplace. Some partners require an AMI for one-click, some allow container images delivered with an ARM/Helm package. We can map to Helios's preference.
[01:20] Ravi Menon: From Helios side we want private deployment in our own VPCs and also a simple 'one-click' deploy option for smaller customers, so likely both. But the AMI path might be heavier for us operationally.
[01:33] Marcus Li: Understood. For the container path we recommend providing: a container registry image (OCI), a Helm chart, a minimal Terraform module, and a sample values file. The Terraform module should handle network attachments and optionally private link. We can validate the module in our CI.
[01:51] Elena Castillo: About the Terraform module, we have an internal network overlay that uses transit gateway and VPC peering. Will Redwood's sample module need to know that?
[01:59] Marcus Li: We don't need the transit specifics, just clear inputs for VPC IDs, subnets, security groups, and an optional field for endpoint type (public/private). If you can share your network diagram, we can advise on parameters.
[02:12] Nina Patel: Elena, can you put that on the action items? Share the network diagram and the Terraform module link.
[02:19] Elena Castillo: Yes, I'll add that. I have a repo at github.com/helios-data/terraform-mod but it's internal. I'll add Redwood to a read-only team.
[02:26] Sofia Alvarez: Quick interjection on security: we need to know what data leaves customer environment. Are logs, telemetry, or prompt payloads sent to Redwood's control plane? We have strict residency requirements.
[02:38] Marcus Li: Important point. For Redwood Private we can offer a control plane inside customer's VPC or a self-hosted control plane. For the hosted option we do collect anonymized telemetry for health, but not prompt content unless opt-in. We can provide the cert matrix and data flows in the security packet.
[02:57] Sofia Alvarez: Okay please share the packet. Also, SOC 2 and ISO attestations are required for our procurement.
[03:05] Nina Patel: We'll attach SOC 2 type II and ISO docs in the security pack. Also include KMS integration notes for customer-managed keys.
[03:12] Ravi Menon: On the pilot, what are the perf expectations? We don't want surprise token costs or latency that breaks our SLOs.
[03:20] Marcus Li: For the pilot we should define a small set of sample workloads with expected request size and concurrency. We'll run perf tests using the same model variants and quantization profile you plan to use. Typical pilot runs 24-72 hours. We'll supply test harness scripts.
[03:36] Tom Brewer: How does licensing/billing work in the listing? We need a metering approach that maps to our SKU model.
[03:42] Nina Patel: Marketplace billing typically supports per-hour instance metering or usage-based metering via API. For Redwood Dedicated or Private, we can support subscription SKUs and metered add-ons. We'll work with your billing PM to ensure the SKU aligns.
[03:56] Tom Brewer: We'll need an example pricing file and a sample marketplace manifest.
[04:00] Nina Patel: We'll send a template for the manifest and sample pricing tiers.
[04:04] Ravi Menon: A thing we've seen with other vendors is that the marketplace certification team wants a hardened image and vulnerability scan report. What's Redwood's stance?
[04:13] Marcus Li: We do a base image scan and recommend a minimal base OS. We can provide the SBOM and scan reports. For AMIs, include Packer templates so customers can rebuild.
[04:24] Elena Castillo: Packer templates would be helpful.
[04:27] Marcus Li: I'll include an example.
[04:29] Nina Patel: Let's go a bit deeper on network and private connectivity. For Private deployments in customer VPCs, how do you want updates applied? Helios uses a change control window for production.
[04:40] Elena Castillo: Yes, we have a weekly maintenance window. We need canary and rollback.
[04:45] Marcus Li: Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic rollback policies. For Private we can do staged deployments using Helm with pre/post hooks and health checks. We'll provide a runbook that shows the commands and validation steps.
[04:58] Sofia Alvarez: Also MFA for admin console and RBAC for tenant separation.
[05:03] Nina Patel: We support SAML/SSO, role-based access controls, and optional audit log forwarding to your SIEM. We'll include config docs.
[05:11] Ravi Menon: Great. On the listing assets, there are logo and marketing requirements. Tom, can Helios provide two variants and a 300x300 PNG?
[05:20] Tom Brewer: Yes we'll provide vector and PNG assets. We'll follow the asset spec you send.
[05:24] Marcus Li: On a slightly different note, any regulatory constraints for EU customers that we should flag?
[05:31] Elena Castillo: Data residency matters for EU customers. For the EU region we need to host control plane components in EU. Also, the marketplace listing needs a region-specific offer.
[05:41] Nina Patel: Noted. We can help with region-specific packaging and documentation.
[05:45] Ravi Menon: On timescales, procurement wants a pilot start in late April and go live in June if all goes well. That's compressed.
[05:53] Marcus Li: That's doable for a small pilot. We'll need the Terraform module and the sample workloads this week or early next to validate.
[06:02] Nina Patel: Okay let's capture concrete next steps. I'll send the checklist, the manifest template, SOC2 and ISO docs, KMS notes, and the sample AMI/Packer and container packaging examples by Friday.
[06:14] Elena Castillo: I'll push the Terraform module and network diagram by Monday. I'll also add Redwood's team to the repo.
[06:21] Tom Brewer: I'll share the marketplace constraints and internal timelines.
[06:25] Sofia Alvarez: I'll review the security packet and follow up with any questions.
[06:30] Marcus Li: For the pilot perf tests, I'll draft the test plan and a script to generate the sample traffic. Expect that by Tuesday.
[06:38] Nina Patel: Awesome. Any blockers or competitor-related constraints we should know?
[06:43] Ravi Menon: We had a procurement hold because BigCloudAI offered a lower sticker price, but their latency was worse in our tests. We'll include those results.
[06:52] Marcus Li: Helpful — if you can share the perf numbers we can compare and tune the quantization profiles.
[06:58] Elena Castillo: One small note — some transcriptions in other calls have misspelled Redwood product names; just to be clear, we mean Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private.
[07:08] Nina Patel: Thanks. We'll reference the right product names in the checklist.
[07:12] Tom Brewer: Any docs links now?
[07:15] Nina Patel: I'll drop a single email with links: listing-checklist.pdf, packaging-examples.tar.gz, manifest-template.yaml, security-packet.zip.
[07:25] Ravi Menon: That works.
[07:28] Nina Patel: Alright let's close with a recap and owners.
[07:32] Marcus Li: Recap: Redwood to send artifacts and perf scripts; Helios to provide Terraform, network diagram, logos; Security to review; schedule pilot kickoff for week of April 20.
[07:45] Elena Castillo: Confirmed.
[07:47] Tom Brewer: Confirmed.
[07:49] Sofia Alvarez: Confirmed.
[07:51] Nina Patel: Thanks everybody. We'll follow up in email and set the pilot kickoff calendar invite once we have dates.
[07:58] Ravi Menon: Thanks, talk soon.

--- End transcript ---
